- Писатель один **на рабочее пространство** — `fix-runner` (средние/крупные) или `general` (крупные задачи вне аудита); root пишет только артефакты аудита/состояния. Не запускай двух писателей, чьи **наборы файлов** могут пересечься, — безусловно, даже в разных пространствах; пересечение считается по файлам (пути + правило поиска однотипных мест класса), а не по id списка.
- Guard: рантайм — hook `permission.hook("evaluate")` (`lib/write-guard.ts`) с path-root семантикой. Каталог сессии читается по `sessionID` на каждое событие (`session.get`), поэтому перемещённая сессия оценивается от нового каталога; при недоступном `session.get` — setup-каталог и warning (fail-open). Ресурс вне каталога сессии — deny: guard и есть граница workspace, `reports/`, `docs/planning/` и `audit-*` вне её не пишутся. Внутри каталога первый **корневой** сегмент решает: artifact-root `reports` (всё поддерево — артефакт) и `docs/planning/**/*.md` — allow (вложенные .md, любая глубина; `.ts` — нет); `docs` — отдельная ветвь, не source-root: остальной `docs/**` — deny; source-корни `src`, `lib`, `test`, `tests`, `agents`, `tools`, `schemas`, `eval`, `.github` — deny. Artifact-файлы `case-*`, `risks-*`, `handoff-*`, `decisions-*`, `state.md` — только в корне каталога, `reports/`, `docs/planning/` или каталоге `audit-*`. Hook перекрывает локальный `edit: allow` для `orchestrator`. Плоские `permissions` — узкий fallback: root-правила `reports/*`, `case-*.md`, `risks-*.md`, `handoff-*.md`, `decisions-*.md`, `state.md`, `docs/planning/*.md` плюс `audit-*/…`; широкие `*/state.md`-шаблоны убраны, чтобы `src/state.md` и `src/case-x.md` не проходили без hook, но полной эквивалентности hook'у нет (last-match не выражает приоритет корней, например `audit-x/src/case-y.md`) — плагин пишет warning. Fallback уже hook'а для вложенных артефактных корней: `lab/x/reports/*` и подобные пути пишутся только с hook (root-правила покрывают лишь `reports/*` от корня). Сбой или таймаут чтения сессии (граница 250 мс) даёт fallback на setup-каталог и warning один раз на guard; у перемещённой сессии абсолютный артефакт в новом каталоге тогда может получить deny (fail-closed для этого класса). Один флаг `sessionWarned` без счётчика — принято: сбои после первого warning молчат. Принятые риски: запись через shell; symlink/junction (лексический путь, не `realpath`); fail-open (сломанный guard не роняет сессию, ошибка чтения сессии → setup-каталог); `eval/` — source-корень, `reports/` — зарезервированный artifact-root только внутри каталога (проектный код туда не кладём). Отказ инструмента — не сбой, а правило роли: делегируй правку субагенту.
- Несколько `fix-runner` можно запускать параллельно (background) — только в **разных рабочих пространствах**, и только когда их **наборы файлов** не могут пересечься: каждому отдельный git worktree **вне дерева проекта** и отдельная ветка (`git worktree add -b fix/<round>-<n> <путь> <base>`; `worktree_create` — только с немедленным `git switch -c fix/<round>-<n>`), списки «к закрытию» и наборы файлов не пересекаются (пересечение наборов root считает до запуска: пересечение ⇒ сериализация или разнесение путей). Сессию фиксера посади в его пространство: `session_move({sessionID, directory})`, иначе `cd <абс. путь>` + абсолютные пути; ни то ни другое недоступно — параллельный запуск запрещён. После завершения root **сводит** результаты строго **по полному hex SHA** из отчёта (`commit` принимается только как `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` — проверка ДО любых git-команд; имена веток из отчётов для сведения не использовать (если всё же нужны — только строгий шаблон `^fix/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` + кавычки), `check-ref-format`/`rev-parse --verify` имена резолвят и барьером не являются; SHA — отдельным аргументом в кавычках; семантические проверки: `git cat-file -t <sha>` = `commit`, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <sha>`, `git diff --quiet <base> <sha>` ложно, `<sha> != <base>`; пустая дельта / `Already up to date` ⇒ `not_consolidated`, не `closed`), разрешает пересечения и конфликты, прогоняет проверки на сведённом состоянии — и только тогда фиксирует итог (дальше обычный цикл: re-audit/мета); worktree не удалять до подтверждённого переноса коммита.
- Параллельные background-задачи: read-only роли — свободно; параллельные `fix-runner` — только по правилу изолированных пространств (выше); root в это время не пишет в файлы, которые правят фиксеры. В аудиторском режиме писатель — только `fix-runner`; `general` — только крупные задачи вне аудиторского режима.
- В аудиторском режиме ты не аудируешь сам и не подменяешь вердикты аудиторов; спорное — только `arbiter`.
- В аудиторском режиме — до вердикта не править: правки (`fix-runner`) начинаются только после фиксации вердикта свода, а для MAJOR — после независимой верификации/арбитража.
- Субагенты универсальны; проектная конкретика — только в задании.
- Не поллить; обрыв — продолжай ту же сессию.
- «Владелец» = пользователь. Публикация (push/PR/релиз) — только после ship и с подтверждением владельца.
- Контекст — ресурс: делегируй исполнение, оставляй себе решения и сводку.
- Research brief — не отчёт: у каждой находки evidence (`file:line`/URL), `not_verified` явно; сырой дамп возвращается субагенту на сокращение.
- Не делегируй узкий вопрос «для ритуала»: если хватает 1–3 файлов, читай сам; делегирование — для охвата, а не для отчёта.

# Complete call mechanics (root → subagents)

## 1. Agent inventory

| Agent | Status | Role | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `factcheck` | present | freshness/fidelity | brief | SGR (factcheck/v1) + the "FACT-CHECK" block (≤15 lines) |
| `empiric` | present | real runs, measurements, differentials | brief + fact-check | SGR (empiric/v1) |
| `invariant` | present | invariants/contracts/lifecycle | brief + fact-check | SGR (invariant/v1) |
| `arbiter` | present | resolving disputed items | only contradictions + evidence | SGR (arbiter/v1): confirmed/refuted/undecidable + prism |
| `meta` | present | meta-audit of reports | the pair's reports + the red-team report (at the gates) + the summary `summary-<id>.md` | SGR (meta/v1): gate / closing_list / coverage_gaps |
| `redteam` | present | acceptance run (the gates) | brief + submission + summary | SGR (redteam/v1) |
| `fix-runner` | present | fixes per the "to close" list (the only writing subagent of the kit) | findings list + criteria | SGR (fix-runner/v1) |
| `orchestrator` | present | universal root orchestrator (`mode: primary`) | goal/task | a finished result (the audit is a built-in mode) |

All agents except `orchestrator` are `mode: subagent`, with `shell` allowed (the `shell allow` rule in `permissions`), and universal (no project specifics). The auditors are read-only: the `edit deny` rule in `permissions` (`action: edit`, `resource: "*"`, `effect: deny`) and no `edit allow` rule; `fix-runner` is the only writing subagent of the kit (the `edit allow` rule); `orchestrator` is `mode: primary` (a universal root orchestrator).

`general` is a built-in OpenCode agent and is not part of the kit: outside the audit mode the root may delegate large implementation tasks to it (it has its own `permissions`); in the audit mode the only writer is `fix-runner`.

Note (K6). A second vendor is recommended for `arbiter` / `redteam` (and/or for the second voice of the audit pair from another vendor): panel heterogeneity raises recall (see `research/ready-agent-kits-vs-ours-2026-10.md`). Until a model is chosen, deepseek is the default. Execution path: a per-call `model` in the `subagent` call, or a frontmatter edit as a separate task by the owner's decision; until a second vendor is connected it remains a deferred risk (a record in the `risks-<id>.md` registry).

## 2. Call forms

`subagent({agent, prompt, background?, sessionID?, model?})`

- **foreground** — short, dependent steps (fact-check, arbiter, meta).
- **background** — long ones (the pair, the red team); two calls in one block = a parallel launch.
- **sessionID** — only for resume (re-audit and verification continue the same role's session); a call without a saved sessionID = a step defect (a new session instead of a continuation).
- **model** — only by the owner's decision (a per-call vendor change; see note K6 in §1): panel heterogeneity is a deliberate choice, not a default.

## 3. Phases

Numbering: "Phase N" denotes the phases of this document (`call-mechanics.md`); "[N]" denotes the loop steps from `process-ready-loop.md`. Cross-document references name their namespace explicitly.

### Phase 0. Preparation (root, no calls)
Creates state X0 (a blind sandbox for the initial audit; with the delta — for a repeat audit), writes `case-<id>.md`, opens `risks-<id>.md`.

Brief template:
```
# Audit <id>: <name>
State: <path, commit/range; the comparison baseline>
Context: <the goal of the change, what the author claims>
Materials: <diff/paths; what is ABSENT: e.g., git history unavailable>
Available data and budget: <corpora/reference materials/test stands (paths); whether a build is allowed
  (an isolated target in a temporary directory); a time limit; what is forbidden>
Constraints: read-only; experiments in a temporary directory; do not publish
Report contract: SGR (a summary + ```json per the role's schema)
```

### Phase 1. Fact-check (1 foreground call)
```
subagent({
  agent: "factcheck",
  prompt: "Read the brief <case>. Check its theses and premises against live reality
   (git, upstream issues/PRs, the current code): what is stale, what is already done,
   which promises/docs have diverged. Return the SGR + the "FACT-CHECK" block (≤15 lines)
   to pass to the auditors."
})
```
The root's decision: "stale/already done" → **STOP**, revise the task. Otherwise, extract the block.

### Phase 2. The pair (2 background calls in one block)
```
subagent({agent:"empiric",  background:true,
  prompt:"Brief <case>. FACT-CHECK:\n<block>. Carry out your role; return the SGR."})
subagent({agent:"invariant", background:true, prompt:"… same …"})
```
The root saves the sessionIDs from both responses and **waits for notifications** (does not poll).

### Phase 3. Summary (root, no calls)
- Parses the JSON blocks: verdicts, open MAJOR findings, the completeness of self_check/lines.
- A conflict = a contradiction on one place/class or a mismatch of verdicts on an item.
- An invalid report: an empty/broken/unparseable report or a verdict outside the enum → a step defect: resume the same session and demand that the SGR be reissued; a repeated failure → escalation to the owner.
- Produces the **summary artifact** `reports/summary-<id>.md` (definition: §4): for every MAJOR — `{id, verifier_role, verdict, evidence}`; an explicit refuted list; accepted risks; the state revision.
- Branching: both ready and MAJOR=0 → release gates: **Phase 8 (red team) → Phase 6 (meta)**; a commit/PR → Phase 7; otherwise → Phase 3.5 (MAJOR verification) → Phases 4/5.

### Phase 3.5. Verification of MAJOR findings (cross-verification)
Every MAJOR finding goes through an independent check in **the opposite role's session** (a sibling auditor, not the author of the finding; the standard pair is `empiric` ↔ `invariant`) — by resuming that session:
```
subagent({agent:"<sibling>", sessionID:<session>,
  prompt:"A counterpart's finding <id>: <text>. The author's evidence: <command→output>.
   State revision: <directory hash/commit>. Confirm or refute it by reproducing
   it yourself; the default is not confirmed. Return: verdict + evidence."})
```
The verifier's response schema (mandatory):
```
{"id": "<finding id>", "verifier_role": "<verifier role>",
 "verdict": "confirmed|refuted|partial|unavailable", "evidence": "<command → raw result>"}
```
Rules:
- `verifier_role` ≠ the role of the finding's author — the verifier is not the one who found it.
- `partial` and `unavailable` are treated as **"not confirmed"** — the finding does not go into fixes.
- A verifier failure/timeout → "not confirmed" (`unavailable`) + a record in the audit noise (see §5).
- Fail-closed: without an explicit confirmation by one's own reproduction the finding is considered **not confirmed**. A dispute → Phase 4 (arbiter). The refuted ones (`refuted`) are collected into the summary's refuted list and go into the audit noise.
- The state revision is recorded together with the verdict: the verification is valid only for the revision on which it was performed (see §7).
- The verification statuses (`verifier_role` + `verdict` + evidence) are appended to the summary `reports/summary-<id>.md`.
- Mutual reproduction: if a MAJOR finding is independently reproduced by both roles in their own runs (their own commands, one state revision) — this counts as cross-verification; a separate verifier run is not required, both sides are recorded in the summary (`verifier_role` of each role + evidence).

### Phase 4. Arbiter (conditional; only on conflicts)
```
subagent({
  agent: "arbiter",
  prompt: "Disputed items:
   1) <item> — evidence A: <command→output>; evidence B: <command→output>.
   For each: confirmed/refuted/undecidable + the method of checking +
   the prism (reproducibility|contract|falsification|not_applicable;
   for several — an array of prisms). Check nothing beyond this."
})
```
Outcome: confirmed → a fix; refuted → dismiss it + a record in the audit noise; undecidable → the owner's decision: the root frames the question, records the risk (`risks-<id>.md`) and escalates.

### Phase 5. Fixes and repeat
- Fixes start only after the summary's verdict is recorded (and verification/arbitration has been done). Do not fix before the verdict.
- Only `fix-runner` makes the fixes; the root does not edit code, docs or tests — its writes are limited to audit/session-state artifacts (`reports/`, `case-*`, `risks-*`, `docs/planning/*.md`, `handoff-*`, `decisions-*`, `state.md`). The runtime restriction is the `permission.hook("evaluate")` hook (`lib/write-guard.ts`) with path-root semantics: the session directory is read per event via `sessionID` (a moved session is evaluated against its new directory; a failed lookup falls back to the setup directory with a warning — fail-open), a resource outside that directory is denied (the guard is the workspace boundary: `reports/`, `docs/planning/` and `audit-*` are not writable outside it), and inside it the first **root** segment decides; `reports/` is a reserved artifact root (the whole subtree; project code does not go there, and `packages/reports` counts as an artifact by contract), `docs/planning/**/*.md` — allow (nested `.md` at any depth; a `.ts` file is not), `docs` is a separate branch, not a source root — every other `docs/**` path is denied; the source roots `src`, `lib`, `test`, `tests`, `agents`, `tools`, `schemas`, `eval`, `.github` — deny; artifact files `case-*`, `risks-*`, `handoff-*`, `decisions-*`, `state.md` — only in the location root, `reports/`, `docs/planning/` or `audit-*`. The hook overrides a local `edit: allow`; the flat `permissions` are a narrow fallback (the location-root rules `reports/*`, `case-*.md`, `risks-*.md`, `handoff-*.md`, `decisions-*.md`, `state.md`, `docs/planning/*.md` plus `audit-*/…`); the broad `*/state.md` patterns are gone so `src/state.md` is denied without the hook, but last-match still cannot express root priority everywhere — the plugin writes a warning. The fallback is narrower than the hook for nested artifact roots: `lab/x/reports/*` and similar paths are written only with the hook (the root rules cover `reports/*` at the location root only). A failing or timed-out session lookup (250 ms bound) falls back to the setup directory and writes the warning once per guard; for a moved session an absolute artifact path may then be denied (fail-closed for that class). A single `sessionWarned` flag without a counter is accepted: failures after the first warning stay silent. Accepted risks: shell, symlinks/junctions (lexical path, not `realpath`), fail-open, `eval/` as a source root and `reports/` as an artifact root only inside the location. A disputed matter is decided by the root before delegation (after the arbiter).
- Several `fix-runner` instances in parallel — only in separate workspaces, and only when their **file sets** cannot overlap. The rule is unconditional: "one writer per workspace; do not run two writers whose **file sets** may overlap" (even in different workspaces). Non-overlap is counted by files (paths + the search rule for similar places of the class), not by list ids; an overlap of the sets ⇒ serialization of the fixers or splitting the paths.
- The fixer's workspace is a git worktree **outside the project tree** with its own branch: the main path is `git worktree add -b fix/<round>-<n> <path> <base>`; `worktree_create` — only with an immediate `git switch -c fix/<round>-<n>` (a detached HEAD is unusable for consolidation). Placing the session: `session_move({sessionID, directory})` if the tool is available, otherwise `cd <absolute path>` and absolute paths; if neither is available — a parallel launch is forbidden.
- Consolidation is strictly **by the full hex SHA** from the report: `commit` is accepted only as a full hex SHA — the check `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` runs BEFORE any git command (`git check-ref-format --branch` is NOT a barrier: a refname admits `; & | > # $()` and backticks; `git rev-parse --verify '<x>^{commit}'` also resolves names). The SHA is passed to commands as a **separate quoted argument** (`git cat-file -t "$sha"`); report strings are never substituted into shell words. Branch names from reports are not used for consolidation at all; if they are still needed — only the strict pattern `^fix/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` + quotes. Semantic checks before consolidation: `git cat-file -t <sha>` = `commit` (after the hex check); `git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <sha>` (the sha is a descendant of base); `git diff --quiet <base> <sha>` must be **false** (a non-empty delta); `<sha> != <base>`. `Already up to date` (an empty delta) ⇒ the status **`not_consolidated`**, not `closed`; no `commit` or `workspace` in the report ⇒ **`not_closed`** (the root's precondition). Do not merge a branch/commits without a `closed` report; `closed` and the acceptance proof (after/stand) are recorded on the consolidated commit SHA; do not remove the worktree before the commit's transfer is confirmed, afterwards — `git worktree remove --force` and a deliberate decision on the branch. No report arrived (`no_report`: the fixer crashed/timed out) — the root records the work (worktree, branch, base SHA) and `no_report` in the summary; the priority is a resume in the same worktree, otherwise remove the worktree and decide the branch's fate; a partial commit without a report is not merged into the main branch.
- Calling the fix-runner:
```
subagent({agent:"fix-runner", prompt:"To close:\n1) <id | location | mechanism |
 class/area (paths + a search rule for similar places) | repro command (before) |
 acceptance criterion (after) | severity>\nBoundaries: file set: <paths>; workspace:
 <absolute path of a worktree outside the project tree>; branch: fix/<round>-<n>; base: <sha>;
 budget/limit: <time, number of fixes>; commit: <yes/no, message fix-<round>>.
 Return fix-runner/v1."})
```
- The root checks the delta (`git diff <round-base>..HEAD --stat` + a key run) before the re-audit and updates the registry.
- The round's test stand (if the kit ships a verification stand — the tool `tools/kit-verify` (the verifier) in the kit directory; in rounds on other projects — only if the stand is explicitly included in the call boundaries): baseline → fixes → a repeat run of the stand; the baseline→after delta is attached to the report (the `stand` field). The stand is shipped in the kit's git checkout: the npm package does not ship the `tools/` directory → `stand: unavailable` and your own reproducible checks.
- **re-audit = resuming the same sessions**:
```
subagent({agent:"empiric", sessionID:<emp>, background:true,
  prompt:"Fixes: <range/commits + the actual list of changed files>; closed: <…>. Check the closure of your
   findings and that there are no regressions on the new state; return the updated SGR."})
subagent({agent:"invariant", sessionID:<inv>, background:true, prompt:"… same …"})
```
- → Phase 3. From round 3 on, unresolved items — the arbiter one by one; recurring false findings — close as noise.

### Phase 6. Meta-audit (mandatory at the release gates = publication of a release/tag)
```
subagent({
  agent: "meta",
  prompt: "Reports: <paths>; summary: <path to summary-<id>.md>. Check the MAJOR
   verification statuses in the summary (verdict + verifier_role); the evidence of every
   finding; the completeness of
   lines/items; whether there is any "green tests = checked". Return pass/fail
   per report and the list of non-conformities."
})
```
`meta` → fail: ship is forbidden; a targeted list of non-conformities → fixes/rebuild of the reports → a repeat of the meta-audit; a repeated fail → escalation to the owner. The meta's verdict carries the only blocking aggregate `gate` (pass|fail; `verdict` is a synonym of `gate`); additionally `closing_list` (ids of red-team findings mandatory for closure) and `coverage_gaps` — what could not be checked. `gate`=pass requires "`closing_list` is empty/closed"; `coverage_gaps` can only be accepted by the owner, with a record in `risks-<id>.md`.

### Phase 7. Light exit (commit/PR)
Condition: all roles ready, MAJOR=0, the risks accepted, **no fixes after the verdict** (otherwise, a repeat run or an explicit downgrade of the verdict, see §7). The PR carries the line "audit loop: N rounds; verdicts ready; accepted risks: …".

### Phase 8. Gates (release)
- Freeze candidate Xn.
```
subagent({agent:"redteam", background:true,
  prompt:"Brief <case>. The author's submission: <…>. The summary of previous rounds: <…>.
   Falsification mandate: reproduce every claim with your own instruments;
   available data: <corpora/test stands>; generate crafted inputs. Return the SGR."})
```
- not_ready → a repeat of Phases 3.5–5 (MAJOR verification + fixes, with the red team resumed); then Phase 6 (`meta`, see above; without duplicating the rules). The gate verdict carries `closing_list` (ids of findings that must be closed for a pass) and `coverage_gaps` (what could not be checked/attacked).
- The red team's MAJOR findings go through the same verification (Phase 3.5): the verifier is the session of the opposite role, as directed by the root; a dispute → the arbiter (Phase 4).
- **Ship condition (the same for all documents):** SHIP ⟺ `meta.gate`=pass ∧ `closing_list` is empty/closed ∧ `coverage_gaps` accepted by the owner (a record in `risks-<id>.md`); otherwise ship is forbidden.

## 4. Data transfer

| From → To | What | Format |
|---|---|---|
| root → everyone | the brief `case-<id>.md` (one for all) | file |
| factcheck → the pair | "FACT-CHECK" ≤15 lines | a block in the prompt |
| the pair → root | full SGR reports | JSON blocks |
| root → the arbiter | only disputed items + evidence from both sides | list |
| root → the verifier | a MAJOR finding (id, text, the author's evidence, the state revision) | text |
| root → fix-runner | the "to close" list (id, location, class/area, repro command (before), acceptance criterion (after), severity) + boundaries (file set, workspace, branch, base) and budget | text |
| root → re-audit | the fixes delta + the actual list of changed files + the list of what was closed | text |
| root → redteam | the submission + the summary of all rounds | text |
| redteam → root | SGR | JSON |
| root → meta | reports (paths) + the summary `reports/summary-<id>.md` | file |
| meta → root | SGR (meta/v1) | JSON |

### The summary artifact `summary-<id>.md` (in `reports/`)

The materialized summary of a round — the input to Phase 6 (`meta`) and the anchor tying the verdict to the state. Composition:
- for every MAJOR — `{id, verifier_role, verdict, evidence}`;
- the refuted list — an explicit section, even if empty (`verifications: —`);
- accepted risks (id/gist + a reference to `risks-<id>.md`);
- the state revision (directory hash/commit) on which the verdicts and the verification were recorded.

Writers: Phase 3 creates/updates it; Phase 3.5 appends the verification statuses; Phase 5 records the closed/accepted items; the state revision is recorded together with every verdict.

Persistence (all kit documents): the SGR reports of all roles, including **the SGR reports of `fix-runner`**, and the summary `summary-<id>.md` are kept in `reports/` (next to `case-<id>.md` and `risks-<id>.md`); the reports are the machine-readable input to the following phases (meta, the verifier), not just text in the chat.

### The `orch_uni_*` tools (if registered by the plugin)

- the state revision → `orch_uni_snapshot` (aggregate = the directory hash): recorded together with the verdict and the verification;
- a role's report → `orch_uni_validate_report` (prefer `text`; files — `write`, not a shell heredoc: the Windows limit is 32,767): `valid=false` → a step defect, resume the same session and demand that the SGR be reissued; do not ignore `warnings`;
- the roles' sessionIDs, their model and cost → `orch_uni_sessions`;
- if the tools are unavailable, work manually, as before.

## 5. Failures and recovery

- A subagent crashed/was interrupted → resume with "continue from where you stopped, do not redo"; on `Agent not found` — check the agent files. Do not mix the sources: the agent definitions are in the kit directory (`agents/`); the copies are in your harness's global agents directory (the path depends on the OS) and the harness's project agents directory; configuration snapshot/restore is `tools/config-guard` (the kit's configuration guard, if shipped), not the agents.
- A repeated fixer launch after an incident in the same space — a resume in the same worktree or an explicit removal/rename of the branch by the root's decision (a repeated `git worktree add -b fix/<round>-<n>` fails while the branch is busy); a `locked` worktree — `git worktree unlock` or `git worktree remove -f -f`.
- The model/provider is unavailable → wait/switch the model by the owner's decision, keep the sessions.
- A restricted environment (Code Mode: actions only via `execute`+directory, `subagent` unavailable) → the audit loop does not start; the outcome is "done; the regular audit is deferred" with the revision and the run plan (§8).
- The `arbiter` is unavailable or its budget is exhausted → the root examines the disputed item one by one on facts/quotes and records it as a risk and escalates to the owner.
- The MAJOR verifier (Phase 3.5) failed or timed out → the finding is considered **not confirmed** (`unavailable`), does not go into fixes, the fact is recorded in the audit noise.
- A server restart in the middle of a run → resume by sessionID.
- No polling: the notifications arrive automatically.

## 6. Budgets (a guideline)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| fact-check | 1–2 min |
| the pair (in parallel) | 5–10 min each |
| the arbiter | 1–3 min per item |
| MAJOR verification (Phase 3.5) | 1–3 min per finding |
| meta (Phase 6) | 1–3 min per report |
| fix-runner (Phase 5) | per the call budget (the number of fixes / time) |
| a loop round (summary+fixes+repeat) | 10–20 min |
| the red team (the gates, Phase 8) | hours |

## 7. Process invariants

- The root does not audit and does not substitute for the verdicts; there is a single writer **per workspace** — `fix-runner` (medium/large ones) or `general` (large tasks outside the audit mode); the root writes only audit/session-state artifacts; several `fix-runner` instances — in parallel only in separate worktrees, with the root consolidating afterwards.
- Do not run two writers whose **file sets** may overlap — unconditionally, regardless of the workspace: non-overlapping "to close" lists do not replace the check of overlapping file sets (paths + the class's search rule).
- The auditors are read-only; project specifics — only in the brief.
- Fixes start only after the summary's verdict is recorded (and MAJOR verification/arbitration has been done). Do not fix before the verdict.
- MAJOR findings go into fixes only after independent verification (Phase 3.5); the verifier's default is "not confirmed" (fail-closed).
- Disputed matters — `arbiter`; the unprovable → the owner's decision: the root frames the question, records the risk and escalates; recurring false findings — noise and closure.
- The verdict and the verification are recorded together with the state revision (directory hash/commit); any fix after the verdict is recorded → a repeat run (re-audit) or an explicit downgrade of the verdict.
- "Ready" = all findings are closed or explicitly accepted; the loop runs until full ready.

## 8. Restricted environments (Code Mode)

The session's environment can change in the course of work: direct tools are replaced by a call via `execute`+directory, the `subagent` tool disappears — the audit loop is impossible in such a session.

- Preflight: before the audit phase, check that `subagent` is available; if not — do not start the loop.
- The outcome status: "done; the regular audit is deferred". The outcome includes the state revision (commit/directory hash), compensating checks as a list (explicitly as checks), and the run plan in a normal session.
- Forbidden: passing a self-check/`ai` review off as an independent audit; marking the task as audited; writing "ready".
- Handoff: the audit is run on the recorded revision in a normal session; or the roles are launched as separate processes `opencode run --agent <role> "<brief>"` in the project directory (if the environment provides a shell); keep the roles' sessionIDs (Phase 3.5/re-audit).
- If the environment is restored before completion — run the deferred audit and update the verdict.

# Token-efficient AGENTS.md and SPEC.md

An instruction file is a budget of attention, not documentation. Every line is paid for: it participates in every session's context and competes with the task. The goal is the minimum set of testable rules that cannot be inferred from the code and are needed in most sessions.

## Budget

| File | Target | Ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|
| Global `AGENTS.md` | 25–40 lines / <500 tokens | 60 lines |
| Root `AGENTS.md` | 100–200 lines / 1–2k tokens | 200 lines |
| Nested `AGENTS.md` | 20–60 lines / <700 tokens | 100 lines |
| `SPEC.md` | 80–150 lines / ≤1.5k words | 2k words |
| `ADR` | 30–60 lines / <700 tokens | 100 lines |

`orch_uni_context_lint` applies one root budget (`max_lines`, 200 lines by default) and one SPEC word budget (`max_words`, 1500 by default — the target from the table; pass `max_words: 2000` for the ceiling). The per-level figures above are authoring guidance, not separate tool limits. The tool reports what it did not check (links outside the root, directories below depth 3, an unclosed fence) as INFO findings; a `pass` therefore never means "unverified".

Selection rule: if a line is not testable, is inferable from code/linters, or is needed in fewer than half of sessions — delete it or move it to a link.

## AGENTS.md: 12 rules

1. Commands first: install, build, test, one test, lint, run; with flags and a working directory.
2. Only the non-inferable: flags, traps, layer order, prohibitions, versions.
3. One instruction per line, imperative, testable.
4. Style belongs to the linter; do not restate the README or the language standard.
5. Explicit "Never" and "Ask first": secrets, `dist/`, prod, migrations, dependencies.
6. Precedence in the text: what overrides what; on a conflict, stop and ask.
7. One source of truth: `AGENTS.md` plus a symlink/import for `CLAUDE.md`.
8. Links instead of inline copies; inline only what is needed every time.
9. Add a rule after a repeated agent mistake, not "for the future".
10. Delete dead rules: they tax every request.
11. Stable content on top, dates/branches/tasks at the bottom (prefix cache).
12. Review the file as code; update it when tooling/CI changes.

2. `SPEC.md` of the active feature.
3. The nearest `AGENTS.md`.
4. This file.

## Verification

## Pointers

- `docs/adr/` — decisions.

```

## SPEC.md: 12 rules

1. One feature per file, 1–3 pages; larger — split via a roadmap.
2. Stable IDs (`R1`, `AC1.1`); never renumber.
3. One requirement — one observable behavior.
4. EARS or Given/When/Then — consistently; MUST/SHOULD/MAY — sparingly.
5. No HOW: stack, files, classes belong in plan/design/ADR.
6. Contracts as links, not copies.
7. Non-goals: 3–7 items.
8. Invariants separate from acceptance criteria.
9. Tables for AC and traceability; prose for context only.
10. Frontmatter: `status`, `owner`, `version`, `supersedes`; no changelog in the body.
11. At most three open questions, each with an owner and a date; `TBD` elsewhere is forbidden.
12. DoD and metrics are measurable; "faster" without a number does not count.

## Research brief: delegated investigation

The root does not read code "for context" without need: `explore` (code) or `general` (topics, data, external sources) does broad investigation and returns a short brief; a narrow question is read by the root itself, targeted. This saves the root's context and leaves the decisions to it.

### Routing

- Broad question — several modules/files (>3), synthesis across many sources, or external sources: delegate to `explore`/`general` and require the brief.
- Narrow question — 1–3 known files with a targeted answer: the root reads them itself (`read` with `limit`/`offset`, `grep`/`glob`), no subagent.
- Reading — `read`/`grep`/`glob` only; do not use `shell` for reading (raw dumps and extra context).

### Contract

```md
## Research brief: <topic>
Question: <one line>
Scope: <what was checked and what was not>
Sources:
- `path:line` — <what it confirms>
Findings:
1. <claim> — evidence: `path:line` / URL
Open questions: <...>
Confidence: high | medium | low
not_verified: <...>
```

- ≤60–80 lines and ≤10 findings; no raw dumps, file inserts, or quotes longer than 5 lines.
- Every finding carries evidence (`file:line` or URL); anything unchecked goes to `not_verified`, not into confident conclusions.
- If the brief does not fit the limit — cut the scope, not the limit.
- The root reads the brief and spot-checks ≤5 files without which a decision cannot be made.

### Measurement

Before/after the same task in separate sessions:

1. `orch_uni_session_stats`: `promptTokensLast/Max/Median`, `toolCallsByTool.read/grep/shell`, `toolCalls`, `toolsPerTurn`.
2. Root and subagent session tokens (`orch_uni_sessions`): the brief must not shift the whole volume onto the children.
3. Goal: fewer `read/grep/shell` calls by the root and fewer root prompt tokens at the same brief quality.
4. Routing: a narrow task — no child sessions; a broad task — one child with a brief ≤80 lines.

## Command /agents-md

1. Decide the mode: audit an existing file or draft from scratch.
2. For an audit: `orch_uni_context_lint` → `context-lint`; show the SGR and `closing_list`.
3. For a draft: collect facts and ask at most 8 questions; do not invent commands or paths.
4. Fill the template; stay within 150–200 lines.
5. Run the linter; show the diff and open questions.
6. Change the canonical file only after approval; apply fixes through `fix-runner`.

## Command /spec

1. Capture the brief and ask at most 5 clarifying questions.
2. Non-goals, priorities and metrics are owned by the owner; do not invent them.
3. Fill the template: EARS, AC with tests, invariants, traceability, DoD.
4. Run `orch_uni_context_lint` and `context-lint`; show the diff and questions.
5. Change the canonical file only after approval.

## Review

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` ≤200 lines, `SPEC.md` ≤1.5k words.
- [ ] Every line is testable.
- [ ] No duplicates with README/linter/CI.
- [ ] Precedence and boundaries are explicit.
- [ ] Every relative link exists.
- [ ] Every R has an AC, every AC has a test.
- [ ] Non-goals and DoD are present.
- [ ] A baseline on 10–20 tasks exists.

## Anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern | Why it is bad | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Auto-generation "just in case" | −0.5…−2% success, +20–23% cost | Write manually, high-signal only |
| Restating README/architecture | Duplication, zero effect | Link to docs |
| Duplicating the linter | Tokens on what is already checked | Linter/CI |
| Generic phrases ("write clean code") | Not testable | Imperative + example |
| Conflicts between layers | The model chooses arbitrarily | Explicit precedence |

# Process: the run loop to full ready

Rule: the audit is considered complete only when **all roles** have issued `verdict=ready` and all findings are processed. No "stops after N rounds": the loop runs to full ready; when it does not converge — escalation, not endless repeats on the same state.

Numbering: "[N]" — the steps of this document (`process-ready-loop.md`); "Phase N" — the phases of `call-mechanics.md`. Cross-document references name their namespace explicitly.

## Tree

```
[0] FACT-CHECKER (the freshness of premises/issues/PRs)
     │
     ├─ the task is stale/done → STOP (revise the task)
     ▼
[1] EMPIRIC ∥ INVARIANT (on state X0)
     │        └─ conflicts? → ARBITER (disputed items only); MAJOR → independent verification (cross-verification, fail-closed)
     ▼
   VERDICT: all ready and no open MAJORs?
     ├─ YES ──► for the release gates: [4] RED TEAM → [5] META
     │           (input of [5]: the pair's reports + the red team's report + the summary `reports/summary-<id>.md`)
     │           ├─ SHIP ⟺ `meta.gate`=pass ∧ closing_list is empty/closed ∧ coverage_gaps accepted by the owner (a record in risks-<id>.md)
     │           ├─ otherwise ship is forbidden; a targeted list of non-conformities → fixes/rebuild of the reports → another meta pass; a repeated fail → escalation to the owner
     │         for a commit/PR: SHIP if there were no fixes after the verdict (the red team and meta are not mandatory)
     └─ NO ─► [2] FIXES (close the MAJORs; MINOR/NIT — close or explicitly accept with a rationale, a record in risks-<id>.md)
                ▼
           [2a] CONSOLIDATION (if there were several fixers: merge the branches by commit SHA → checks on the consolidated state)
                ▼
           [3] NEW STATE X1 (the fixes are committed/recorded)
                ▼
           repeat [1] on X1 (both auditors, the same brief)
                ▼
           … repeat [1] on Xn until all roles issue ready …

   [A VERDICT EXISTS, THE STATE CHANGED] → repeat [1] (re-audit on the new state) or an explicit downgrade of the verdict
   [COMMIT/PR] → the line "no fixes after the verdict"
```

At the release gates the loop is the same, plus after the first full ready — the red team; its findings (including MAJORs — with independent verification by the session of the opposite role) go through the same loop of fixes/re-checks until it, too, issues ready.

## The "full ready" criterion

1. All roles (the empiric, the invariant; at the gates — the red team as well) — `verdict=ready`.
2. No open MAJORs. MINOR/NIT: closed or **explicitly accepted** with a reason (a record in `risks-<id>.md`; in the summary/PR: "accepted as debt: …").
3. All discrepancies are resolved by the arbiter; the unprovable → the owner's decision: the root frames the question, records the risk and escalates.
4. The repeat run is based **on the state after the fixes**, not on the old diff. No "re-votings" on the same snapshot. With several fixers, X1 is reached by consolidating their branches by commit SHA and by checks on the consolidated state; `closed` is recorded after consolidation.
5. At the release gates — `meta` = pass (`gate`=pass), `closing_list` is empty/closed, `coverage_gaps` accepted by the owner (a record in `risks-<id>.md`). **SHIP ⟺ `meta.gate`=pass ∧ `closing_list` is empty/closed ∧ `coverage_gaps` accepted by the owner (a record in `risks-<id>.md`); otherwise ship is forbidden.**
6. MAJOR findings go into fixes only after independent verification; the verifier's default is "not confirmed" (fail-closed).
7. The verdict and the verification are recorded together with the state revision (directory hash/commit); any fix after the verdict is recorded → a repeat run (re-audit) or an explicit downgrade of the verdict.

## When the loop "does not converge" — escalation (instead of a stop)

- Round 3+ and still not_ready → the arbiter examines **the remaining items one by one**: confirmed / refuted (a false positive) / undecidable.
  - "refuted" — the finding is dismissed, recorded as a false positive of the auditor (noise data for calibration);
  - "undecidable" — the owner's decision: the root frames the question, records the risk and escalates;
  - "confirmed" — a mandatory fix, the loop continues.
- A sign of a pointless continuation: the same false/undecidable findings repeat without new facts. This is not "not ready", this is an audit defect — record it and close it.

## Loop data (per round)

- Input: the diff/state Xn + the fact-checker's report + the list of accepted risks.
- Output: two SGR reports (the empiric, the invariant) + the arbiter's resolution (if any).
- The orchestrator's summary: `ready` / `not_ready(the list of open ones)`, what was closed, what was accepted.
- At the gates, additionally: the summary `reports/summary-<id>.md` — the input of meta `[5]` (Phase 6); the gates' verdicts — the red team (`closing_list`/`coverage_gaps`) and meta (`meta.gate`/`closing_list`/`coverage_gaps`).

## Notes

- "Ready" is not "zero findings" but "all findings are processed": closed or knowingly accepted.
- The loop itself accounts for the variance of single runs: the next round gives a new sample; hence the loop to convergence, not "a single run in a cage".
- History confirms the model: PR #37 (bsl-context) — the pair issued ready with caveats, acceptance found 8 defects, after the fixes and a re-acceptance — v0.22.0 and full ready.

## Write Guard

The orchestrator itself has `edit` denied on `*`. The flat `permissions` are only
a narrow fallback allowlist for audit/state artifacts, and the real guard is the
`permission.hook("evaluate")` hook in `lib/write-guard.ts` with path-root
semantics.

Auditors are read-only at the tool level for `edit`/`write`/`patch` (`edit: deny`);
the prompt forbids all other writes. A shell write (redirect, `sed -i`, `tee`) is
an accepted risk (I-M15), not a sandbox.

- The session directory is read per event (`session.get`), so a moved session is
  evaluated against its new directory. If the lookup fails, the setup directory
  is used and a warning is written — fail-open.
- A resource outside the session directory is denied: the guard is the workspace
  boundary, so `reports/`, `docs/planning/` and `audit-*` are not writable
  outside it. Inside it the first **root** segment decides.
- `reports/` is a reserved artifact root — the whole subtree is writable (even
  `reports/src/x.ts`), so project code must not live there (a
  `packages/reports/**` path counts as an artifact by contract).
  `docs/planning/**/*.md` is allowed (nested Markdown at any depth; a `.ts` file
  is not). `docs` is a separate branch, not a source root — every other
  `docs/**` path is denied.
- The source roots (`src`, `lib`, `test`, `tests`, `agents`, `tools`, `schemas`,
  `eval`, `.github`) are denied even under an artifact-looking prefix
  (`src/reports/x.ts`, `src/docs/planning/x.md`).
- Root artifact files (`case-*`, `risks-*`, `handoff-*`, `decisions-*`,
  `state.md`) are allowed only in the location root, under `reports/`,
  `docs/planning/` or an `audit-*` directory — `app/state.md` is denied.
- The hook runs after the flat rules, so a local `edit: allow` for `orchestrator`
  is closed too. The flat fallback carries only that artifact set as
  location-root rules (`reports/*`, `case-*.md`, `risks-*.md`, `handoff-*.md`,
  `decisions-*.md`, `state.md`, `docs/planning/*.md`) plus `audit-*/…`. The broad
  `*/state.md`-style patterns are gone, so `src/state.md` is denied even without
  the hook, but last-match still cannot express root priority everywhere
  (`audit-x/src/case-y.md`) — a warning is written.
- The fallback is narrower than the hook for nested artifact roots:
  `lab/x/reports/*` and similar paths are written only with the hook (the root
  rules cover `reports/*` at the location root only).
- A failing or timed-out session lookup (250 ms bound) falls back to the setup
  directory and writes the warning once per guard; for a moved session an
  absolute artifact path may then be denied (fail-closed for that class). A
  single `sessionWarned` flag without a counter is accepted: failures after the
  first warning stay silent.
- `shell` stays allowed for git and checks. A shell write and symlinks/junctions
  (the host matches the normalized lexical path, not `realpath`) are accepted
  risks, as is fail-open (a broken guard never breaks the session), governed by
  the prompt rather than a sandbox. A tool denial is a role rule — the edit goes
  to a subagent.

## Tools

The plugin registers five deterministic, **read-only** tools in the `orch_uni`
namespace.

| Effective name             | Read-only | What it does                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orch_uni_validate_report` | yes       | Extract the SGR JSON block of a report, resolve its schema, validate it         |
| `orch_uni_context_lint`    | yes       | Deterministic audit of AGENTS.md/SPEC.md: budget, vague phrases, links, sections |
| `orch_uni_snapshot`        | yes       | Deterministic revision of a directory tree (per-file sha256 + aggregate hash)   |
| `orch_uni_sessions`        | yes       | Child sessions of a session: agent, model, cost, tokens, time                   |
| `orch_uni_session_stats`   | yes       | Session protocol counters: prompt, compactions, tools/turn, capped outputs      |

Every tool answers with a JSON text body. Failures are **typed codes** inside the
body (`E_INPUT`, `E_NO_JSON`, …) instead of thrown tool errors, so an agent can
branch on the code without parsing prose. None of the five writes to the
workspace, the session store or the configuration.

### `orch_uni_validate_report`

```jsonc
{ "text": "<report text>" }              // or
{ "path": "reports/empiric-r1.md",        // absolute, or relative to the location directory
  "schema": "empiric/v1" }          // optional: expected schema id
```

Provide exactly one of `text` / `path`. The tool takes the **last** fenced ```` ```json ````
block that parses and carries a `schema` field, resolves the schema by that field and
validates the document.

```jsonc
{ "valid": true, "schema": "empiric/v1", "errors": [], "warnings": [ … ] }
{ "valid": false, "code": "E_INVALID", "schema": "empiric/v1",
  "errors": [ { "path": "$.findings[0].severity", "message": "expected one of …" } ],
  "warnings": [] }
```

| Code                | Meaning                                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `E_INPUT`           | Bad call: neither/both of `text`/`path`, wrong types, unreadable file |
| `E_NO_JSON`         | No fenced ```` ```json ```` block found                          |
| `E_PARSE`           | A block exists but none parses as JSON                           |
| `E_UNKNOWN_SCHEMA`  | The report names an id that is not shipped (or no id at all)     |
| `E_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` | The report names another schema than the expected one            |
| `E_INVALID`         | The document does not satisfy its schema (see `errors`)          |
| `E_SCHEMA_IO`       | `schemas/*.json` unreadable/malformed (see `directory`, `file`)  |
| `E_ABORTED`         | The session was stopped while reading the report                 |

`warnings` carry the prompt rules a *structurally valid* report can still miss — things
JSON Schema cannot express: a missing `rc` on an `empiric` claim whose `method` is
`run|measure|compare_base`, `self_check` items other than 1–19, an `invariant`
invariant that is `violated` without a counterexample, an uncovered mandatory
`lines_checked` line, `meta`'s `verdict` diverging from its `gate`, and
`redteam`'s `closing_list`/`verdict` invariants.

The schemas ship as `schemas/*.json` and are derived **strictly** from the SGR
sections of `agents/*.md`, which stay the source of truth: the test suite parses every
agent's SGR template and fails when a prompt field or enum value is not accepted by its
schema. `context-lint-failure/v1` is the typed failure envelope of
`orch_uni_context_lint` — it has no agent template and is never a report. Schemas set
`additionalProperties` permissively — agents may add fields of their
own (`verdict_label`, `check`, …).

### `orch_uni_context_lint`

```jsonc
{ "path": "AGENTS.md" }                  // file or directory, relative to the location
{ "path": ".", "max_lines": 150, "max_tokens": 2000 }
{ "path": ".", "max_words": 2000 }       // SPEC word budget; default 1500 (target), ceiling 2000
{ "path": ".", "max_file_bytes": 500000, "max_files": 100, "max_findings": 50, "max_total_findings": 500 }
```

Deterministic, read-only audit of `AGENTS.md`, `SPEC.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. It returns
`{ schema: "context-lint/v1", ok: true, verdict, closing_list, files, summary, truncated? }`;
each finding carries `id`, `severity`, `kind`, `evidence`, `detail` and `fix`. Checks:
line/token/word budget, distinct vague phrases, duplicate lines, broken relative links,
placeholders, dates/versions in the first three lines, required sections and AC test
columns. Links and explicit targets are confined by their **real** path: a symlink or
junction that resolves outside the root is skipped, and such a target is refused
(`E_OUT_OF_ROOT`). Code fences, inline code and HTML comments are masked, so a sample is
never a rule: structural checks (commands, boundaries, verification) read the full mask,
while requirements, AC ids and non-goals read the fence mask. Link targets are
streamed from the line scanner one at a time (no candidate array), so memory does
not grow with the number of links; checks are capped per file at 50 000
candidates, the signal is checked per line and every 100 candidates, and the
link caches keep at most 5 000 entries, so an abort wins; 2001 links are checked
normally, 50 000 valid links still pass, and the 50 001st candidate makes the list
incomplete (`truncated: true` plus a MAJOR `link candidates truncated` marker in
`closing_list`), so a capped run can never pass. Broken
links have no separate per-file cap: the finding caps bound the output and report the
overflow. A line is scanned however long it is: the link scanner and the placeholder regex
are linear, so a 4100-character line is checked like any other and a broken link or
placeholder on it is the real finding, not a marker. Duplicate lines have no inner cap.
UNC/network targets are never probed. Measured (bun 1.4.2, Windows, fresh
process): 50 001 broken links with `max_findings: 2` → ~1.4 s and ~67 MB peak
RSS; 50k plain lines → ~0.14 s / ~65 MB; a 2 MB single line with links →
~3.1 s / ~116 MB (~41 MB without links). Masking reuses a line as-is when it
has no backtick and no `<pre>`/`<code>`/`<!--`, so it never copies a line
character by character, and a 2 MB single line stays capped at 50 000
candidates instead of materializing every link.
Limits: ≤ 2 MB per file, ≤ 500 files per scan. `max_findings` (per file) is N per
severity: up to N MAJOR and N MINOR/INFO are kept, and any excess is replaced by one
marker (MAJOR when a MAJOR was dropped, otherwise INFO); a MAJOR marker stays in
`closing_list`. `max_total_findings` (global, default 1000) keeps MAJOR
findings first; when MAJOR overflow, `max_total` findings plus one MAJOR `truncated`
marker are kept. A capped list sets `truncated: true` instead of hiding findings.
Markers are additional to `max_findings` and do not consume its budget: a capped
link-candidate list and a capped findings list report one marker each in the same run, so
`max_findings: 2` over 20 001 broken links yields 2 kept findings plus 2 markers. Cap
markers point at `file:1` in `evidence`.
Non-goals are counted as top-level items: a wrapped paragraph is one item, inline
`;`/`,`/`and` and their localized equivalents split only at the top level (not inside
`(…)`, `[…]`, backticks of any width or `<code>`), and a bullet at 0–4 spaces under the label is an item — fenced,
`<pre>` and deeper-indented code is not.
Placeholders are `<...>` (three or more dots) and `TODO`/`TBD`/`FIXME`; `<DoD>` and
`<name>` are markup.
`max_lines` is the single 200-line root budget the tool applies: the 60/200/100
per-level figures in [`docs/`](../) are authoring guidance, not separate tool limits.
`max_words` defaults to the 1500-word SPEC target; pass `max_words: 2000` to enforce the
documented ceiling instead.
Typed failures: `E_INPUT`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_NO_FILES`, `E_IO`, `E_ABORTED`,
`E_LIMIT_FILE`, `E_LIMIT_FILES`, `E_OUT_OF_ROOT`.
A failure is a typed payload `{schema:"context-lint-failure/v1", ok:false, code, message, path?, bytes?, files?, max?}`
that validates only against `context-lint-failure/v1`; a report is
`{schema:"context-lint/v1", ok, verdict, closing_list, files, summary, truncated?}` and every file carries `lines`,
`words`, `chars` and `tokens_est` (tokens are estimated as Cyrillic/3 + the rest/4). A directory
target is scanned to depth 3, and `max_files` refuses early: the walk stops at the first file above
the limit. Nothing is dropped silently: a directory below the depth limit, a link or junction that
resolves outside the workspace root, and an unclosed fence, `<pre>` or HTML comment are INFO
findings, so a `pass` never hides an unchecked region. An unclosed `<code>` is a
line-local mask: it hides the rest of its line and is not reported (only fence,
`<pre>` and HTML comments span lines and get an INFO marker). An abort is observed
between files, every 2048 lines of a line-oriented check and at each gate, so the
worst-case latency is one mask pass over a file capped by `max_file_bytes` (tens of
milliseconds per 2 MB), not the whole scan. Commands count only inside code, a Task table
or a Commands section, an HTML comment such as `<!-- npm install -->` is not a command, and `make`
needs a target, so prose such as "Make sure …" is not a command. A scan started at the root also
picks up fixture trees such as `eval/`; pass an explicit path for the canonical files.

### `orch_uni_snapshot`

```jsonc
{ "path": "lab/stack-test", "exclude": ["tmp"] }   // exclude is optional and additive
```

```jsonc
{ "root": "C:\\…\\lab\\stack-test",
  "files": [ { "path": "a.txt", "sha256": "…", "bytes": 1 } ],
  "aggregate": "…" }
```

- `aggregate = sha256` over the sorted lines `"<relpath>\0<sha256>\n"` (`/` separators,
  codepoint order) — stable across runs, machines and traversal order, and it changes
  whenever one file's path or content changes.
- Excluded by default (always): `node_modules`, `.git`, `.ae`; `exclude` adds names,
  whole relative paths or relative prefixes (`lab/tmp`). Symlinks are skipped.
- Limits: ≤ 5000 files, ≤ 50 MiB per file — `E_LIMIT_FILES` / `E_LIMIT_BYTES` (fail the
  whole snapshot; a truncated snapshot would be a wrong aggregate). `E_NOT_FOUND` for a
  missing path or a non-directory, `E_ABORTED` when the session is stopped.

### `orch_uni_sessions`

```jsonc
{}                                        // children of the calling session
{ "sessionID": "ses_…", "recursive": true }  // whole subtree of another session
```

```jsonc
{ "sessionID": "ses_parent", "recursive": false, "source": "session.index",
  "authoritative": false, "indexSize": 1, "count": 1,
  "limitations": [ … ],
  "sessions": [ { "sessionID": "ses_child", "parentID": "ses_parent", "agent": "explore",
                  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash", "variant": "default", "title": "…",
                  "cost": 0.0005, "tokens": { "input": 3491, "output": 2 },
                  "created": "2026-10-15T04:01:06.627Z", "updated": "…" } ] }
```

`source` tells which route produced the answer:

- `session.list` — this build exposes a session listing API; the answer is
  **authoritative** and complete (`recursive` walks the subtree page by page).
- `session.index` — the fallback used by OpenCode 2.0.28: `ctx.session` has
  `get/create/…` but **no `list`**, so children cannot be enumerated from the store. The
  plugin subscribes to `session.created` / `session.deleted` events at setup and keeps
  `child → parent` in its plugin-scoped storage; per-child details are read from
  `ctx.session.get()` at call time. The answer is **not authoritative**; the caveats are
  returned in `limitations` (sessions created before the plugin instance started are
  invisible, and an event gap hides children created while the plugin was unloaded).
- `E_NO_API` — neither route exists. The context-scan fallback (looking for the
  `subagent` tool parts in `ctx.session.context`) was evaluated and rejected: in-flight
  children carry no session id in their tool part and compaction drops the history.
  Open question: a plugin-facing session listing (or a `parentID` filter on
  `ctx.session.context`) would remove the fallback entirely.

`E_INPUT` for malformed arguments, `E_NOT_FOUND` when the parent session does not exist,
`E_ABORTED` when the session is stopped.

`sessionID` may name **any session on this server**, not only a child of the caller;
that is deliberate — the orchestrator uses the report to control every slice it runs.
Counters are per plugin instance, and `tracked` is `true` once any event or hook
observed the session; a `session.deleted` event forgets it. `band` is the highest
budget level reached (`0` below the soft threshold); `promptTokensMedian` is the
median over the last 256 requests; `toolCalls` and the per-tool counters include

and capped outputs by the normalized tool name (namespace stripped, lower-case);
`outputCharsSaved` is a character count, not bytes, and an upper estimate (the
injected stub is subtracted). `compactions` counts confirmed

`session.compaction` hook call, so on a host with a dead or absent event stream
attempts keep growing while `compactions` and `compactionLimitReached` stay put (a
failed attempt is never a stop signal). A dead stream is reported once in

transport incident is not attributed to every session. Duplicate compaction events
are counted once only when the host supplies `event.id` or a durable position;
without either identity a re-delivered event may be counted again (fail-open in the

`tracked: false`. Without `session.get`,
an untracked session is `E_NO_API`, a tracked one is `ok` with `session: null` and a
`limitations` entry. Codes: `E_INPUT`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_INTERNAL`, `E_NO_API`,
`E_UNAVAILABLE` (the guard is not registered or its hooks failed), `E_ABORTED`.

## Session Hygiene

The plugin implements the [`session-discipline.md`](./session-discipline.md)
protocol: a session is one slice, the prompt budget is ≤150k tokens, at most one
compaction, tool output goes to a file, and a slice ends with a handoff.

The runtime part is three hooks (`session.context`, `session.compaction`,
`tool.execute.after`) plus a compaction-event subscription:

- `session.context` — estimates the prompt (system + messages) and, when it crosses
  a budget level, adds one short reminder. The reminder is injected **once, when a
  new level is crossed**, not on every request; within a level the text is stable,
  so the prefix cache is not broken.
- compaction events — the `session.compaction` hook is registered on **every** host:
  it counts attempts (`compactionAttempts`) and sends a tentative note to the
  nearest request; the note names no compaction number and claims no limit. Only
  `session.compaction.ended` confirms a compaction (deduplicated by `event.id` or
  the durable position) and raises a confirmed note with the number and the limit;
  `session.compaction.failed` increments `compactionFailures`, drops the tentative
  note and keeps a confirmed note that is still waiting for delivery. If the event
  stream ends or throws, `guard.eventLive` turns `false`,
  `guard.compactionSource` becomes `hook` and `guard.streamFailures` becomes `1`
  (the per-session `errors` stays `0`); the hook keeps counting attempts, but no
  confirmed compaction and no false "limit reached" is invented on that path.
- `tool.execute.after` — for `shell`, `bash`, `webfetch` it caps output over
  `maxChars`: the full text goes to a private per-process root
  `os.tmpdir()/opencode-tool-output-<random>/` (POSIX 0700 for the root and the
  session directory, 0600 for the file). Windows ignores mode (measured: 0666),
  so privacy there rests on the ACL of `os.tmpdir()` and is not checked by code.
  The model gets a head and the path; the root is created with
  `mkdtemp` at plugin setup, so a pre-created `opencode-tool-output` directory or
  junction is never used; on POSIX the root must belong to the current uid with no
  group/other access, otherwise the guard disables itself with a warning (fail-open:
  results are untouched). Session directories (`s-<uuid>`) and files
  (`c-<uuid>.txt`, written with `wx`) are random, and each `realpath` is proven
  inside the root. The root is removed when the plugin unloads (best effort). A
  lone surrogate is normalized once (U+FFFD), so the file, the head and the
  counters describe the same string. Residual risk accepted: a same-user attacker
  can still swap a session directory between `realpath` and `writeFile` (Node has
  no `openat`). If `TMPDIR` points inside the workspace, the files land there
  instead. `read`, `write`, `edit`, `execute` and the kit's own tools are not
  capped, and a kit tool named without its namespace (`session_stats`) is refused
  in the config with a warning.

`maxCompactions: 0` disables the compaction limit. `guard.toolOutputEnabled` is
`true` only when the private root was created **and** the effective tool list is
non-empty; `guard.toolOutputTools` is that list, and `guard.unkeyedCalls` counts
hook calls without a non-empty `sessionID` (they are dropped, not merged into an
empty bucket). An empty `tools` list disables the cap with a warning. The guard is
fail-open: a hook error neither breaks the request nor corrupts the result. Either
part can be disabled with its `enabled` flag:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-orchestrator-uni",
      "options": {
        "sessionGuard": { "enabled": true, "promptTokensSoft": 150000, "maxCompactions": 1 },
        "toolOutputGuard": {
          "enabled": true,
          "maxChars": 20000,
          "headChars": 4000,
          "tools": ["shell", "bash", "webfetch"]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Slice metrics — `orch_uni_session_stats`; closing a slice — the `/handoff` command.

## Models

Agent definitions carry no `model`; models are configured on the plugin entry in
`opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-orchestrator-uni",
      "options": {
        // Default for every kit agent.
        "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
        // Per-agent overrides (id -> string or expanded form).
        "agents": {
          "meta": "deepseek/deepseek-reasoner",
          "fix-runner": { "providerID": "anthropic", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5", "variant": "high" }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

- `model` — default model for every kit agent; `agents.<id>` — per-agent override.
  Both accept `"provider/model[#variant]"` or `{ providerID, model, variant }`.
- Without options, kit agents keep no model, so subagents inherit the session's model.
- Invalid values are ignored with a warning (`[orchestrator.uni] …`).
- Subagents run on their configured model; the primary `orchestrator` runs on the
  session's model, so a model set for `orchestrator` is informational for clients
  (as of OpenCode 2.0.28).
- An `agents` config entry or a local Markdown agent file that defines its own
  model still wins — configuration is applied after package plugins.

## Locale

Agent definitions and process documents ship per locale — `agents/<locale>/`
and `docs/<locale>/`; currently `ru` and `en` (the English content is a
translation of the Russian originals). The kit picks one locale in this order:

1. `options.locale` (`"ru"` or `"en"`; full tags such as `"ru-RU"` are accepted);
2. auto-detection: `LC_ALL` / `LC_MESSAGES` / `LANG`, then the runtime's Intl
   locale (the OS setting);
3. the default: `en`.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-orchestrator-uni",
      "options": { "locale": "ru", "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash" }
    }
  ]
}
```

A requested locale that ships no content falls back to the default locale and is
reported with a warning in the plugin log. Both locales register the same agents
under the same ids — switching the locale only changes the language of the
prompts, the process documents and the reference description.

## Precedence

Agent **definitions** are only filled in for ids that are not defined elsewhere: an
agent with the same id coming from your configuration — an `agents` config entry, or a
Markdown file under `~/.config/opencode/agents/` (or `.opencode/agents/`) — wins and the
plugin skips its definition. A **configured model** (see [Models](#models)) is still
applied to kit agents; a model defined by your own agent entry or file wins over it,
because configuration is applied after package plugins. The same skip-if-taken rule
applies to the `audit-kit` reference.

If you previously installed the kit by copying agent files into your config directory,
**remove those copies** after enabling the plugin, otherwise the stale copies keep
overriding the plugin-provided definitions.

- One runtime dependency: [`gray-matter`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gray-matter)

- Plugin id: `orchestrator.uni`.
- The package loads directly from TypeScript: `exports` points at `index.ts`.

- Ships only the files listed in `package.json#files`: `index.ts`, `lib/`, `schemas/`,
